title: PR garden weeder — quick notes and heuristics
content:
Context: quick personal scratch for triaging small PRs during sprint. Not a team doc — rapid heuristics, half-formed refactor sketches, and explicit follow-ups to turn into issues. Save for later: convert high-confidence items into PR templates or checklist bot rules.

Goals:
- Reduce PR churn on small surface API changes.
- Make low-risk refactors easier to merge without long review cycles.
- Capture follow-ups so we don't carry context in reviewers' heads.

Quick review heuristics (fast filter — decide in 10–15m):
1) Scope check — is this a single behavioral change or a bundle? If bundle -> ask author to split.
2) Tests present? If not, is change trivial (typo/docs) or risky (logic/interaction/serialization)? For anything that touches serialization/DB/contract -> require test.
3) API contract: does this modify any public API or client-facing surface? If yes -> check migration notes and versioning.
4) Perf/alloc: any new per-request allocation or heavy loops? Flag for perf bench if >1ms per request expected.
5) Security/data: does code touch PII/logging/headers? If yes -> escalate to security review.
6) Non-blocking nitpicks: use suggestions (GH review) or leave short comments; avoid bikeshedding in small PRs.

Fast checklist template I keep in comments for reviewers:
- [ ] Scope small and well-scoped
- [ ] Behavior covered by tests or trivial change
- [ ] No public contract change (or migration plan included)
- [ ] No amplification of failure modes / graceful fallback
- [ ] Logging/metrics updated if behavior changes
- [ ] Docs/README updated if developer-facing

Refactor idea sketches (short notes):
A) Thin adapter for KV cache layer
- Problem: multiple callers construct the same cache-key tuple in slightly different orders.
- Idea: add a small adapter that accepts a canonical struct and exposes builder helpers.
- Rollout: add adapter internally, convert 2–3 hot callers in same PR, run integration. Keep internal-only flag for 1 week then convert rest.
- Risks: surface churn in callers; plan small, incremental conversions.

B) Route-level small-batch harness (local)
- Problem: unit tests for batching logic are brittle when running with real threads.
- Idea: provide a harness that simulates batching windows deterministically (time mocks) to make logic deterministic and remove flaky tests.
- Follow-up: add harness tests to failing flaky suite (see flaky-suite label).

C) Lightweight invariants for ModelConfig objects
- Introduce a Validate() method returning []string issues instead of throwing; this makes validation testable and composable across code paths.

Follow-ups / possible issues to file (convert to tickets):
- PLAT-1776: Standardize cache-key builder for kv-cache (owner: Diego) — include migration plan and compatibility tests.
- Micro: add deterministic batching harness and migrate two flaky tests (owner: Maya).
- Add a tiny PR-lint rule: block merges when files named "*_schema.go" change without schema-version bump in CHANGELOG.md. (owner: me)

Tests to add (explicit):
- deterministic batching harness unit tests: 3 cases (empty window, multi-request, overflow).
- ModelConfig Validate() property tests: missing fields, conflicting fields, edge sizes.
- Serialization roundtrip test for new adapter (kv keys must roundtrip identical).

Common review phrases I use (save as canned comments):
- "Scope seems broad — can this be split into two focused changes?"
- "Please add a test exercising the failure-case described in the comment."
- "Nit: consider extracting X into a small helper to improve readability and reuse."

Merge safety rules (my personal rules for small merges):
- If PR < 30 LOC and only comments/docs -> self-merge after CI green.
- If PR touches public API surface (anything in /api/ or exported methods) -> require 2 reviewers and release note.
- If PR introduces a new dependency -> run quick license check and brief perf smoke.

Short-term experiment ideas (one-week spikes):
- Auto-suggest split: bot comments with suggested boundary lines when PR has >3 unrelated file changes.
- Review 'fastpath' label: author can request 1-reviewer merge if all tests stable and PR <50 LOC and owner is senior on team. Monitor incidents for 2 sprints.

Open questions (to resolve with team or in sync):
- What counts as "public API" in platform repo (need precise file/path rules)?
- Acceptable lag for converting internal callers to new adapter — 1 week or 2?

Notes to self (action list):
- Today: add canned GH comments for the top 5 repeated review phrases.
- This week: file PLAT-1776 and attach short migration checklist.
- Next sprint: prototype deterministic batching harness, push as draft PR and ask QA to run flaky-suite.

Random quick wins (low effort):
- Add small README in kv-cache dir explaining canonical key ordering (2–3 lines).
- Add unit test template file under internal/testutils/time_mocks.go and reference in README.

If I forget, blame the coffee.

-- end scratchpad --
